subject: Archetype AI — request to reprofile Dedicated capacity ahead of renewal
messages:
From: Elena Varela <elena@archetypeai.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@archetypeai.com
Date: 2026-09-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reprofiling Dedicated ahead of renewal — sustained GPU pressure

Hi Maya —

We're about a month out from our renewal and we've seen steady changes in production workload after the new retrieval model shipped. Over the past 45 days our 32 x A100(80GB) Dedicated pool is showing a higher baseline: steady-state utilization around 58–65% with frequent 2–6 minute bursts that push queue latency up beyond our 250ms SLO. We ran the attached utilization export (archetype-utilization-q3-2026.csv) and added brief notes in the sheet.

We want to avoid customer-facing latency during this period but also keep a tight budget. Options we discussed internally: (1) add 16 GPUs to the Dedicated commit, (2) add a 24-GPU burst pool, or (3) convert 8 of our Dedicated slots to a higher-throughput instance (H100 equivalent) for the most expensive endpoints.

Can you help scope what each option looks like from throughput, estimated monthly cost, and operational impact (rollout, pinning, fallbacks)? Also if there are short-term mitigations (KV prefix caching, per-route batching) your side recommends, we'd like to try those before a full commit add.

Thanks — Elena
Ops Lead, Archetype AI

Attachments: archetype-utilization-q3-2026.csv (CSV export from Console)
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
To: Elena Varela <elena@archetypeai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reprofiling Dedicated ahead of renewal — sustained GPU pressure

Elena —

Thanks for the data and summary. I pulled the CSV into our console and sketched an options matrix. High level thoughts:

- Add 16 A100(80GB) to Dedicated: simplest operationally, predictable throughput increase (~50–60% headroom), tightest SLA profile. Estimated incremental cost: ~USD 46k/mo (ballpark; final depends on term).
- 24-GPU burst pool: lower committed spend, supports spikes but doesn't improve steady-state latency because of preemption/queueing model. Best if spikes are short and infrequent.
- Convert 8 slots to H100-equivalent: improves p99 token throughput on heavy-decoder workloads; useful if latency is token-bound. This requires a model-variant pin and test window — operationally slightly more complex.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (no infra change): enable route-level KV prefix caching for your embed->rerank calls, and set per-model max_batch_latency to 5ms for critical routes (we can push via your private config). Those typically recover 15–30% of p99 tail in workloads like yours.

I'll loop Ben and Karthik to propose a concrete amendment we can send for signature (DocuSign) and to validate capacity scheduling. Can you confirm which option you prefer to prioritize and whether you want a 12- or 24-month term?

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: proposed-capacity-amendment-ARC-2026-09.pdf (draft)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reprofiling Dedicated ahead of renewal — sustained GPU pressure

Maya/Karthik —

Quick ops/forecast notes for Maya to include in the amendment:

- Current commit: 32 x A100(80GB) (region: us-west-2), avg sustained tokens/sec consistent with 60% utilization for Q3.
- If customer adds +16 A100s (same family), we can guarantee <2% throttling during observed 30-day patterns and remove burst backlog in ~95% of observed surges. Schedule: new tranche can be live in ~7 business days after signed amendment.
- If they prefer a mixed approach (8 A100 + 8 H100), ops will need a 14-business-day validation window to test model-variant pinning and kernel selection; recommend a canary rollout for 48 hours.
- Cost sensitivity: 12-month term gives ~12% discount on list; 24-month gives ~18%.

I'll attach a simple cost table and a one-pager for the migration steps to the amendment. Note: if they choose burst-only, we should propose an integrated autoscale policy to avoid double-charging over short repeated spikes.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
From: Elena Varela <elena@archetypeai.com>
To: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@archetypeai.com
Date: 2026-09-05T16:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reprofiling Dedicated ahead of renewal — sustained GPU pressure

Thanks, Maya/Ben —

We reviewed the options with finance/infra. Plan and asks:

1) Prioritize adding 16 A100s to Dedicated on a 12-month term (we want deterministic throughput).
2) Schedule a short config change: enable KV prefix caching for top-3 routes and set max_batch_latency for those routes to 5ms — we understand this is reversible.
3) Please send the amended contract with the 12-month pricing and DocuSign link.

We want the new capacity live before the traffic spike we expect on Sep 20. Is that feasible?

Elena

Attachment: archetype-utilization-q3-2026.csv (updated note added)
From: maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-08T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reprofiling Dedicated ahead of renewal — sustained GPU pressure

Elena —

Great — thanks for confirming. Next steps:

1) We've attached the amendment and DocuSign packet (docusign-topup-ARC-2026-09.pdf) and set the term to 12 months with the 12% list discount. Please review and sign; DocuSign link also in related_links.
2) Ops notes: Ben confirms we can have +16 A100s active in us-west-2 within 7 business days of signed agreement. We'll schedule the KV caching + batch-latency flip during the same maintenance window and run a 48-hour observability sweep.
3) I'll add a rollback playbook and a canary flag for the busiest route; Karthik will own the rollout and share runbook on the shared Drive folder.

If you sign today we can target Sep 17 as the go-live to provide a buffer before Sep 20.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping the service smooth.

Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
